item.title: Same Technology, Different Problems? A Comparative Bibliometric Analysis of Generative AI Across Education, Business, Communication, and Governance
item.description:
methaodos revista de ciencias sociales
The rapid diffusion of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) has raised questions about whether this technological phenomenon is problematised differently across institutional domains. This study compares GenAI scholarship in education, business and organisational research, communication and media and public governance, law, and policy. Four domain-specific Web of Science Core Collection corpora for 2023–2026 comprised 6,132, 1,901, 300 and 444 documents, respectively. Bibliometric performance analysis, thematic mapping, and author-keyword co-occurrence analysis were conducted using Bibliometrix/Biblioshiny and VOSviewer. Distinct thematic configurations emerged across the four domains. Education foregrounds learning, assessment, AI literacy, and academic integrity. Business research emphasises innovation, technology adoption, decision making, and organisational capability. Communication scholarship centres on journalism, trust, disinformation, and informational credibility, whereas research on governance foregrounds regulation, accountability, rights, and legal responsibility. These patterns are not treated as direct measures of institutional logics. Instead, the study develops a theory-informed mapping that relates empirical thematic configurations to institutional problems and normative priorities. GenAI is not problematised uniformly; its institutional salience is shaped by divergent criteria of legitimate knowledge, organisational value, professional authority, and public accountability. The study offers a comparative framework for examining GenAI as an institutionally situated sociotechnical phenomenon while maintaining a clear distinction between bibliometric evidence and institutional interpretation.

item.title: Ramping-up hippocampal ripples and their neocortical coupling support human visual short-term memory
item.description:
[预印本] eLife
Emerging evidence suggests that the hippocampus contributes to visual short-term memory (VSTM). However, the neural mechanisms through which hippocampal activity supports the maintenance of VSTM representations remain largely unknown. Here, using intracranial EEG recordings from human participants performing a delayed match-to-sample task for naturalistic objects, we investigated the role of hippocampal ripple activity—brief high-frequency oscillations associated with memory replay—in VSTM maintenance and hippocampal-neocortical communication. We found that hippocampal ripple rates progressively ramped up during the maintenance period and supported successful VSTM. More critically, hippocampal ripples were temporally coupled with the ripples in the lateral temporal lobe (LTL), and these coupled ripples were associated with memory reactivation in the LTL. These findings provide direct evidence that hippocampal–neocortical interaction via coupled ripples supports VSTM, extending the role of hippocampal ripples from long-term consolidation to short-term mnemonic processes and offering new insights into the dynamic coding mechanisms of working memory.

item.title: Explainable Artificial Intelligence for Improving Transparency and Reliability in Automated Decision-Making Systems
item.description:
Computer Science Bulletin
Automated decision-making systems increasingly influence healthcare, finance, recruitment, education, public administration, and digital platforms. Although advanced machine-learning models can discover complex relationships, their opaque reasoning can obstruct auditing, contestability, and safe deployment. This narrative review examines how explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) may improve transparency and reliability by clarifying model behavior, revealing data dependencies, supporting error detection, and enabling informed human oversight. It synthesizes established work on interpretable modeling, local feature attribution, surrogate explanations, counterfactual reasoning, explanation evaluation, and governance. A conceptual assurance framework connects data provenance, predictive validation, explanation fidelity, subgroup analysis, and operational monitoring. The paper distinguishes understandable explanations from evidence that a system is accurate, robust, or fair: an attractive explanation alone does not establish reliability. A non-empirical diagram illustrates complementary assurance dimensions without implying measured results. Practical implications include tailoring explanations to decision recipients, testing explanation stability under perturbations, documenting uncertainty, and establishing appeal mechanisms. The review concludes that XAI is most effective when embedded within a wider socio-technical accountability process rather than deployed as a stand-alone visualization technique.

item.title: Big data and artificial intelligence in digital marketing
item.description:
Bizinfo Blace
Big Data and artificial intelligence are changing digital marketing through consumer behavior analysis, personalized communication, and automation. This paper examines their role in marketing processes, performance measurement, and the conditions for application in Serbia. A narrative review of selected literature is combined with a descriptive analysis of published statistics on ICT use, e-commerce, and enterprise AI adoption. The analysis identifies widespread consumer participation in digital channels alongside more limited enterprise adoption of AI. Serbia remains below the EU average in enterprise AI use, although above some member states. The paper’s contribution lies in linking data resources, analytical capabilities, and managerial competencies to explain why technology adoption alone is insufficient for effective digital marketing. Practical implications emphasize employee development, responsible data management, and the evaluation of marketing outcomes. The findings should be interpreted within the limits of aggregate indicators, which do not directly measure marketing-specific AI use or its effectiveness. Future research should examine these applications and their outcomes at the enterprise level.

item.title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN EDUCATION: OPPORTUNITIES, CHALLENGES, AND PEDAGOGICAL PERSPECTIVES
item.description:
来源未提供
Artificial intelligence (AI) is becoming an increasingly important element of educational innovation. AI-based tools offer opportunities to personalize learning, support teachers in preparing instructional materials, provide timely feedback, and improve access to educational resources. At the same time, their implementation raises concerns related to academic integrity, data privacy, algorithmic bias, and the development of students' independent thinking. This paper examines the pedagogical opportunities and limitations of AI in education through a theoretical analysis of relevant international policy documents and research publications. It argues that effective integration of AI requires a human-centred approach, appropriate teacher training, ethical guidelines, and the preservation of meaningful interaction between teachers and learners. AI should be considered a supportive educational resource rather than a replacement for professional pedagogical judgement.

item.title: Tutoría Basada en Inteligencia Artificial para Fortalecer el Razonamiento Proporcional en Estudiantes de Primer Semestre
item.description:
Erevna Research Reports
Justification: Deficiencies in proportional reasoning with which students enter higher education affect the understanding of more complex content; therefore, pedagogical strategies are required to help overcome these difficulties. Objective: To evaluate the effectiveness of artificial intelligence–based tutoring in strengthening proportional reasoning among first-semester students at a public university in the province of Manabí, Ecuador. Methodology: A quantitative approach with a descriptive-comparative scope was adopted, using a pre-experimental pretest–posttest design with two groups. The sample consisted of 78 students. The intervention involved tutoring supported by artificial intelligence tools, structured in two stages: prior knowledge construction and proportional problem solving. Data were collected using two performance tests designed to assess the identification, structuring, and application of proportional relationships. Results: After the pedagogical intervention, the results showed a shift toward higher performance levels in both groups, with a reduction in the low level and a significant increase in the high level. Specifically, improvements were observed in the identification, structuring, and application of proportional relationships; however, the change in identification was less pronounced. Inferential analyses revealed statistically significant differences between the pretest and posttest (p < .001), with large effect sizes. Conclusion: Artificial intelligence–based tutoring strengthened proportional reasoning among the first-semester students who participated in this study.

item.title: Effect of Trust in AI on Human AI Relationship among University Students
item.description:
Pakistan Journal of Positive Psychology
The study aimed to examine the effect of trust in AI on Human-AI relationship among university students. A cross-sectional survey research design was used. The sample comprised 300 university students (150 males and 150 females) selected through convenient sampling technique. Measures included the General Attitude toward AI Scale (GAAIS) by Schepman and Rodway (32 items, Positive α = .84, Negative α = .73), Short Trust in Automation Scale (S-TIAS) by McGrath et al. (3 items, α = .88), and Experiences in Human-AI Relationships Scale (EHARS) by Yang and Oshio (7 items). Correlation analysis showed that trust in AI was positively correlated with Human-AI relationship. The study contributed to the growing literature on Human-AI relationships by highlighting the role of trust in AI in Human-AI interactions among university students. The findings have important implications for AI literacy, technology acceptance, and the development of educational interventions aimed at fostering healthy and effective Human-AI relationships.

item.title: Teacher Mediation of AI Use and Learning Autonomy at SMP Negeri 4 Pekanbaru
item.description:
Indonesian Journal of Educational Innovation
Generative artificial intelligence (AI) expands access to information and instructional support while raising concerns about information accuracy, cognitive dependence, and learning autonomy. This study examines how teachers mediate AI use while strengthening students’ independent learning at SMP Negeri 4 Pekanbaru. A qualitative case study was conducted in August 2026 with five purposively selected informants: one school principal, three subject teachers, and one Grade VIII student. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews and supporting documentation and analyzed using thematic analysis. The findings reveal several interconnected patterns: AI functions as a learning assistant; teachers validate AI-generated information; structured tasks maintain students’ cognitive engagement; digital-device use is regulated according to instructional purposes; and teachers increasingly act as facilitators, mentors, validators, learning designers, and technology regulators. The study proposes a teacher-mediated AI balance in which access to AI is followed by teacher guidance, verification, independent processing, and learner accountability. This pattern offers a practical framework for integrating AI while sustaining reasoning, responsibility, and self-regulated learning in junior secondary education.

item.title: Artificial Intelligence as a Catalyst for Sustainable Development and Business Transformation: A Conceptual Study
item.description:
International Journal on Research and Development - A Management Review
Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly positioned at the intersection of business transformation and sustainable development. Its capacity to identify patterns in large datasets, forecast demand and risk, automate routine processes, support product innovation, and improve resource allocation creates opportunities to enhance organizational performance while addressing environmental and social priorities. Yet these outcomes are not automatic: AI can reproduce bias, intensify surveillance, displace or transform work, widen digital inequalities, and consume substantial energy and material resources. This conceptual study synthesizes the supplied literature review on AI-enabled sustainability, digital transformation, innovation, governance, and the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). It develops an integrated framework in which AI capabilities influence sustainable business transformation through three complementary mechanisms: operational and resource optimization, innovation capability, and data-driven decision-making. The proposed framework links AI adoption with economic, environmental, and social sustainability through digital infrastructure, workforce skills, organizational readiness, and collaboration. Responsible governance, fairness, accountability, and data protection ensure ethical implementation. AI-driven sustainability requires strategic alignment, organizational learning, and responsible practices to achieve measurable business transformation and sustainable outcomes. As a conceptual paper, it does not claim empirical validation; instead, it offers propositions and a research agenda for future survey, case-study, and structural-equation modelling research.

item.title: The Role of Artificial Intelligence in Modern Business Management: A Conceptual Study of Opportunities and Challenges
item.description:
International Journal on Research and Development - A Management Review
Artificial intelligence (AI) has moved from the periphery of experimental computing to the centre of managerial practice, reshaping how organisations make decisions, allocate resources, engage customers and manage people. Despite the rapid growth of scholarship on the subject, the literature remains fragmented across functional silos, and the opportunities and risks of AI are frequently examined in isolation from one another. This conceptual study synthesises existing literature to examine the role of AI in modern business management and to articulate an integrated understanding of its opportunities and challenges. Drawing on the technology–organisation–environment framework, the resource-based view, dynamic capabilities theory and the automation–augmentation perspective, the paper develops a conceptual model comprising five interrelated components: AI adoption enablers, AI applications across management functions, the dual effects of AI (opportunities and challenges), organisational outcomes, and moderating governance mechanisms. The model proposes that AI generates sustainable value only when technological capability is matched by organisational readiness, responsible governance, effective human–AI collaboration and continuous workforce development. The discussion elaborates the implications of the model for strategic decision-making, operations, marketing, human resource management and finance, and considers the ethical, social and implementation challenges that accompany adoption. The paper contributes a theoretically grounded and integrative framework that can guide future empirical research and support managers who seek to adopt AI responsibly and effectively.

item.title: Fintech-Driven Transformation of Financial Markets and Investment Decision-Making: A Conceptual Study
item.description:
International Journal on Research and Development - A Management Review
Financial technology (fintech) is changing how financial markets operate and how investors access, interpret, and act on financial information. Digital payments, mobile investment platforms, robo-advisory services, artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning, big-data analytics, blockchain, and automated trading have altered the speed, reach, and informational basis of financial decisions. Yet the consequences are not uniformly beneficial: greater access and analytical capacity can coexist with cyber risk, algorithmic opacity, behavioural overconfidence, platform dependence, and unequal digital capabilities. This conceptual study synthesizes the literature review supplied for the paper, which covers fintech adoption, digital transformation in financial services, capital-market infrastructure, AI-supported investment decisions, financial risk management, mutual-fund choice, and the behavioural implications of personal-finance applications. The study proposes an integrated conceptual model linking fintech capabilities to investment decision-making quality through information accessibility, analytical support, transaction efficiency, and trust. Behavioural biases act as mediators, while financial literacy, digital capability, and governance quality moderate the proposed relationships. Expected outcomes include decision quality, portfolio alignment, participation, and market efficiency, subject to risks and institutional conditions. The model is conceptual and is not presented as empirically validated. It offers propositions for future testing and practical implications for investors, fintech providers, financial institutions, and regulators. The central argument is that fintech creates value when technological capability is combined with informed users, transparent design, robust safeguards, and meaningful human oversight.

item.title: When Does Nature Become Therapy? Reconsidering Therapeutic Experience, Agency, Professional Guidance, and Commercialisation in Shinrin-Yoku, Forest Bathing and Forest Therapy
item.description:
Shinrin-Yoku Journal
The term therapy is increasingly employed across practices concerned with human well-being, including music therapy, sound therapy, aromatherapy, nature therapy, forest therapy, and Shinrin-Yoku. However, its meaning varies considerably across clinical, scientific, cultural, professional, and commercial contexts. An experience may be perceived as therapeutic without constituting a formal therapeutic intervention, just as a service may be marketed as therapy without possessing an established clinical methodology or clearly demonstrated therapeutic efficacy. This article critically examines the meaning and implications of therapy within forest-based practices. Drawing on research in environmental psychology, public health, forest medicine, sociology, nature connectedness, and therapeutic relationships, alongside Japanese historical developments and the author’s previous conceptual work, the discussion questions where therapeutic agency resides. Is it the forest environment, the guide, the participant, the social context, or the interactions among these elements that make an experience therapeutic? The analysis distinguishes between therapeutic effects, therapeutic intentions, organised well-being interventions, and clinically delivered treatments. It further considers the evolution of Shinrin-Yoku into contemporary forest therapy terminology, the value and limitations of professional guidance, relational approaches to forest engagement, and the commercialisation of nature-based experiences. Particular attention is given to the possibility that meaningful and restorative experiences can emerge through ordinary, unstructured contact with nature, without professional guidance or explicit therapeutic intention. The article proposes a relational and context-sensitive understanding of therapeutic experience, supported by principles of co-creation, co-responsibility, and co-being. Rather than seeking a universal definition of forest therapy, the discussion advocates greater conceptual precision, professional transparency, methodological pluralism, and critical reflection. It concludes that the therapeutic potential of an experience cannot be adequately determined by its name, setting, or professional structure alone. Keywords: Shinrin-Yoku; forest bathing; forest therapy; nature therapy; therapeutic experience; nature-based interventions; therapeutic agency; forest therapy guides; relational well-being; commercialisation; medicalisation; nature connectedness

item.title: The leading role of technological factors in the development of the global online education market
item.description:
World Economy and World Finance
The article analyzes the leading role of technological factors in the development of the global online education market. The impact of the spread of the Worldwide Web, mobile devices, cloud services, artificial intelligence, e-learning, personalization of learning, virtual and augmented reality, information security, big data, and gamification of learning on the transformation of the educational environment is considered. It is shown that digital technologies have accelerated the transition from traditional forms of education to online formats, expanded access to educational resources, and made learning more flexible, personalized, and scalable. Special attention is paid to how technological innovations are changing the models of interaction between students and educational platforms, improving the quality of content and creating new mechanisms for evaluating learning outcomes. The growth factors of the online education market are also considered, including the development of digital infrastructure, increasing the investment attractiveness of the EdTech sector and the growing demand for distance education services. The paper emphasizes that technological factors are not only a condition, but also the main driver of further expansion of the global online education market. It is concluded that the further development of this field will be determined by the speed of innovation and the ability of educational organizations to adapt to digital transformation.

item.title: Handcrafted Feature Extraction and Classification for Distinguishing Real and AI-Generated Images
item.description:
The Journal of Applied Technology and Innovation
The generative machine-learning approaches are extensively used to create artificial images. These images are called AI-generated images. The AI-generated images find applications like rapid content creation, creative design and visualization, rapid prototyping, etc. In spite of many applications, the AI-generated images are leading to issues like bias, copyright issues, deepfakes, etc. Owing to the importance of discriminating between synthetic and real images, many research approaches have been proposed. Among these methods, deep learning approaches are popular. However, the design of common deep learning detection approaches to detect the synthetic images that are generated by different generative models is a challenging task. There are issues with these methods to discriminate images that are subjected to various pre-processing steps. To overcome these issues, machine learning approaches with the handcrafted features are gaining importance. In this context, five types of handcrafted feature extraction and random forest-based classification is proposed to distinguish between AI-generated and real images. The simulation experiments are carried out with AI-generated and real facial images, with each group having 70,000 samples. Out of 70,000 samples from each group, 50,000, 10,000, and 10,000 samples are respectively used for training, validating, and testing the classifier. The performance of the classifier is evaluated for accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score. The recognition accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 scores of 86.03%, 86.15%, 85.87%, and 86.01%, respectively, are achieved for three feature combinations

item.title: The Concise Language Paradigm in left and right hemisphere stroke: a longitudinal source-localized EEG study
item.description:
[预印本] bioRxiv (Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory)
The mechanisms underlying language recovery after stroke remain poorly understood. Most previous studies have either focused on language comprehension or production and/or relied on hemodynamic measures, with limited complementary electrophysiological evidence. Here, we combined the Concise Language Paradigm (CLaP), assessing comprehension and production, with individualized electroencephalography (EEG) source reconstruction to investigate post-stroke language function and changes in hemispheric dominance over time. In two sessions, we tested stroke-free controls, individuals with left hemisphere (LH) or right hemisphere (RH) stroke. Participants with stroke were assessed two and seven months post-stroke. EEG data were analyzed using event-related potentials and time-frequency representations, followed by source reconstruction based on state-of-the-art individual MRI-derived forward models. Laterality indices were calculated to assess changes in hemispheric dominance between sessions. Behaviorally, the LH group showed low performance at two months followed by overall improvement, whereas the RH group mainly improved in functional communication. EEG activity was significantly modulated by task condition across comprehension and production contrasts. Source-level results in controls were consistent with established language-related networks, serving as regions of interest for the stroke analyses. In the stroke groups, hemispheric dominance differed between LH and RH stroke participants, with LH participants showing systematic shifts from left- to right-hemisphere dominance between sessions, if not already right-hemisphere dominant at two months. Our study provides evidence on comprehension and production performance after stroke using a single paradigm. These findings demonstrate dynamic changes in hemispheric dominance during post-stroke recovery, ultimately highlighting the value of individualized EEG source reconstruction to investigate post-stroke plasticity.

item.title: Functional and Structural Neuroanatomic Correlates of Intraoperative Anesthetic Dose-Adjusted EEG Alpha Power Among Older Surgical Patients
item.description:
[预印本] medRxiv
Background: Alterations in intraoperative electroencephalography (EEG) alpha power and anesthetic dose-adjusted EEG alpha power (ADA-FP alpha power) have been associated with both preoperative cognitive impairment and postoperative delirium (POD) among older surgical patients, yet the neurologic underpinnings of alterations in these anesthetic brain response patterns are unknown. Methods: We conducted a single center prospective observational cohort study (ALADDIN), of older adults undergoing non-cardiac/non-cranial surgery, which included preoperative structural and resting state functional MRI, lumbar punctures to obtain CSF, 32 channel intraoperative EEG recordings, and repeated POD assessments. To account for anesthetic dose, frontoparietal EEG alpha power (ADA-FP alpha power) was adjusted using our established formula: [intraoperative alpha power]/(2.5 - end-tidal MAC fraction). Multivoxel pattern analysis (MVPA) with follow-up seed-to-voxel analyses identified functional connectivity patterns associated with intraoperative ADA-FP alpha power. Voxel-wise regression analysis with threshold free cluster estimation (TFCE) correction was used to evaluate associations between cortical thickness and ADA-FP alpha power. CSF biomarker values were obtained from NULISA proximity extension assays. Delirium incidence and severity was assessed with the 3-Minute Diagnostic Confusion Assessment Method (3D-CAM). Delirium severity area under the curve (AUC) during hospitalization was defined as the sum of all 3D-CAM delirium severity scores within the postoperative hospitalization period (for up to 7 days after surgery). The Confusion Assessment Method for the Intensive Care Unit (CAM-ICU) was used in cases of non-verbal/intubated patients. Results: ALADDIN enrolled 215 patients, of whom 168 underwent surgery and had high-quality intraoperative EEG data (44.6% female; mean age 70.9 years). MVPA showed that ADA-FP alpha power was associated with altered functional connectivity within the bilateral frontal poles, left superior frontal gyrus and the right superior parietal lobule (p-FWE < 0.05). Seed-to-voxel analyses revealed that higher ADA-FP alpha power was associated with increased connectivity between DMN MVPA regions and DMN, DAN and salience/ventral attention and decreased connectivity with visual regions. Conversely, right superior parietal lobule connectivity shifted towards greater DMN segregation and increased somatosensory/motor coupling (p-FWE < 0.05). Lower ADA-FP alpha power was also associated with lower cortical thickness in left occipitotemporal and superior parietal cortices (TFCE-corrected p < 0.05). ADA-FP alpha power was also lower among participants with (vs those without) postoperative ward/floor delirium (mean difference, 1.33; 95% CI, 0.22 to 2.44; p=0.019), and ADA-FP alpha power was inversely associated with peak delirium severity (spearman's rho = -0.26; 95% CI, -0.40 to -0.11; p <0.001) and delirium severity AUC (spearman's rho = -0.28; 95% CI, -0.42 to -0.13; p < 0.001). Discussion: These findings suggest a functional and structural neuroanatomic basis for the decreased EEG ADA-FP alpha power values seen among some older surgical patients, which may explain the association between decreased EEG ADA-FP alpha power and increased rates of both preoperative cognitive impairment and postoperative delirium. More specifically, these findings suggest that altered default mode and dorsal attention network connectivity is linked to decreased EEG ADA-FP alpha power and raise the possibility that preoperative/baseline functional connectivity alterations within these networks may play a role in delirium risk.

item.title: Single-Case Design for Network-based BCI Rehabilitation: Individual Learning Trajectories and Effects of Motor Imagery Timing in Stroke Patients
item.description:
[预印本] medRxiv
Motor imagery (MI) brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) are increasingly investigated for promoting motor recovery after stroke. However, it remains unclear how BCI control improves through repeated training in stroke patients and whether the timing of MI decoding systematically influences this trajectory. To address this question, we implemented a single-case experimental design involving five chronic stroke patients enrolling in a longitudinal electroencephalography MI-BCI training involving their affected hand. Across 18 sessions conducted over six weeks, the onset of a fixed-duration MI decoding window was randomized to occur 1, 2, or 3~s after cue onset according to an alternating-treatments single-case design. Notably, the BCI combined spectral power and functional connectivity features to classify MI states. The MI classification timing had no significant effect on BCI accuracy, fatigue, or spasticity. BCI accuracy increased across training in four of five patients and was accompanied by patient-specific longitudinal changes in local spectral activity and functional connectivity. These convergent trajectories were consistent with acquisition of BCI control, but were not accompanied by clinically meaningful improvement in motor function. Varying the onset of the MI decoding window provided no systematic benefit for BCI control. Instead, differences in neurophysiological trajectories across patients indicate that MI decoding parameters need to be personalized and reassessed throughout the training. Overall, these findings inform more individualized and effective BCI settings for neuromotor stroke rehabilitation.

item.title: Biology Undergraduates Use of AI-Enabled Feedback to Revise Scientific Writing: Recipience and Barriers
item.description:
[预印本] bioRxiv (Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory)
Background: Instructors and education researchers are increasingly developing feedback with the assistance of generative AI, which we refer to as AI-enabled feedback, yet we do not know whether established understandings of feedback uptake and effectiveness apply similarly in AI-mediated contexts. This makes the recipience of AI-enabled feedback a central concern to understanding how to best support students in developing their scientific writing skills. This study examined how two teams of undergraduate biology students used AI-enabled feedback to revise their scientific writing, and the extent to which their revisions addressed that feedback. The teams revised their research proposal drafts after receiving AI-enabled feedback developed by their instructor with the aid of a custom AI tool. Results: Our findings show that AI-enabled feedback prompted actionable revision across both teams. Each team addressed approximately half of the feedback comments, indicating comparable levels of uptake despite their differing approaches to revision. We observed that both teams were inconsistent in providing the additional information and reasoning requested in the feedback, and they struggled to address comments requiring self-evaluation. Taken together, we see that students often addressed the more easily actionable parts of AI-enabled feedback while omitting more demanding revisions. Conclusions: These findings provide behavioral evidence of how students used AI-enabled feedback to revise their scientific writing. The observed patterns suggest that the content of AI-enabled feedback supported meaningful revision, while limitations in students agency, strategies, and volition likely shaped their implementation of comments. Although the degree of uptake observed in this study is encouraging, it is unlikely that a single application of generative AI within the feedback process will resolve all the challenges associated with feedback uptake.

item.title: Readiness of Teacher Educators to Adopt Artificial Intelligence in Teaching and Learning: A Narrative Integrative Review
item.description:
The Paradigm Chronicle Journal of Academic Inquiry and Critical Thought
Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly influencing teaching, learning, assessment and professional development in higher education. Teacher educators occupy a significant position in this transformation because they prepare prospective teachers to respond to changing educational practices and technological demands. However, the successful integration of AI into teacher education requires more than access to digital tools. It depends on educators’ technological knowledge, pedagogical competence, ethical awareness, professional confidence and institutional support. This paper examines the readiness of teacher educators to adopt AI in teaching and learning through a narrative integrative review of selected scholarly literature and international policy frameworks. The review draws on research concerning AI in education, generative AI, technological pedagogical knowledge and teacher professional development, alongside UNESCO’s guidance and competency framework. The synthesis is organised around five dimensions of readiness: technological and AI literacy, pedagogical integration, ethical and responsible use, professional learning, and institutional preparedness. The review highlights the importance of continuous professional development, supportive institutional policies, critical evaluation of AI-generated content and the preservation of teacher agency. It proposes a multidimensional conceptual framework for understanding teacher educators’ readiness and identifies priorities for future empirical research, particularly in diverse and resource-constrained teacher education contexts. The paper concludes that meaningful AI adoption requires a human-centred, pedagogically informed and institutionally supported approach.

item.title: Evaluating the effectiveness of AI-Based adaptive learning for reading development and self-regulated learning among pupils with dyslexia in Abuja, Nigeria
item.description:
Aminu Kano Academic Scholars Association Multidisciplinary Journal
Children with dyslexia often experience persistent challenges in reading, motivation, and self-regulation within traditional classroom settings that rely on uniform instructional approaches. With the growing integration of artificial intelligence in education, AI-based adaptive learning systems have emerged as innovative tools capable of personalizing instruction and supporting diverse learning needs. This study investigated the effect of AI-based adaptive learning systems on reading performance, motivation, and self-regulation among primary school students with dyslexia in Abuja, Nigeria. A quasi-experimental pretest–posttest control group design was adopted, with a sample of 60 Primary 5 pupils drawn from selected inclusive and special education schools in the Abuja Municipal Area. Data were collected using a Reading Performance Test, Motivation toward Reading Scale, and Self-Regulation in Reading Questionnaire, and analyzed using descriptive and inferential statistics, including independent samples t-test. Findings revealed that students exposed to AI-based adaptive learning demonstrated significantly higher improvements across all variables compared to those receiving conventional instruction. The experimental group recorded substantial gains in reading performance (mean gain = 24.20), motivation (mean gain = 1.50), and self-regulation (mean gain = 1.60), compared to the control group. Statistical analysis confirmed that these differences were significant (p < 0.05). These findings align with Cognitive Load Theory, Self-Determination Theory, and Vygotsky’s Zone of Proximal Development. The study concludes that AI-based adaptive learning systems offer an effective approach for improving both academic and psychological outcomes among students with dyslexia. It recommends the integration of AI-driven instructional tools in primary education, alongside teacher training and policy support, to promote inclusive, personalized, and effective learning environments.

item.title: Pemetaan Struktur Intelektual dan Evolusi Tematik Penelitian Pendidikan: Sebuah Analisis Bibliometrik
item.description:
JURNAL PENELITIAN DAN EVALUASI PENDIDIKAN
This study examines the intellectual structure and thematic evolution of educational research through bibliometric analysis. Using bibliographic records retrieved from Scopus on September 19, 2026, the study initially identified 4,090 publications covering the period from 1906 to 2026. The analysis combined bibliometric performance analysis and science mapping to investigate publication trends, leading sources, author contributions, geographical distribution, document types, subject areas, and keyword relationships. VOSviewer was employed to generate network, overlay, and density visualizations of keyword co-occurrence patterns. The findings indicate an expansion of scholarly publications in recent years, with the United States and the United Kingdom representing major geographical contributors. Social Sciences and Arts and Humanities constitute prominent subject areas, reflecting the interdisciplinary character of educational research. Keyword mapping identifies education, teaching, learning, curriculum, and educational theory as central concepts connected to specialized themes, including educational technology, artificial intelligence, critical pedagogy, social justice, and professional education. By integrating publication indicators with thematic mapping, this study provides an overview of the knowledge organization and thematic diversity represented in the retrieved literature. The findings offer a reference for identifying established research areas, exploring interdisciplinary connections, and formulating future research directions. However, the results should be interpreted in light of the search strategy, metadata availability, and incomplete publication year of 2026

item.title: A Survey-Based Study on the Adoption of Generative AI in Software Development: Opportunities, Challenges, and User Perspectives
item.description:
Iconic Research and Engineering Journals
Generative AI (GenAI) is increasingly used in software development for coding, debugging, documentation, and learning. This study examines its adoption, benefits, challenges, security concerns, dependence, learning support, and future impact. Survey responses from 21 programming students and professionals were analyzed using frequencies, percentages, and average ratings. Of the respondents, 95.2% reported daily or frequent use and 95.2% used ChatGPT. Debugging and error fixing was the most common task (71.4%). Respondents reported benefits such as better problem-solving and faster development, but also identified bugs, security issues, architectural complexity, and privacy concerns. Overall, GenAI is viewed as a useful assistant, but human review, testing, and responsible use remain essential. The findings are exploratory due to the small sample size.

item.title: Transforming Global Early Childhood Education Through Artificial Intelligence: Addressing Teacher Shortages, Inequality, and Quality Gaps in Early Learning Systems
item.description:
International Social Research Nexus (ISRN)
This study examines the potential of artificial intelligence (AI) to support early childhood education (ECE) in addressing workforce pressures, inequality, and quality-related challenges, while identifying the organisational, pedagogical, and ethical conditions required for responsible AI use. An interpretivist qualitative design was used with 22 participants (8 head teachers and 14 early childhood teachers) from ECE institutions in Sydney, Australia, who took part in semi-structured face-to-face interviews. Six interconnected themes emerged from inductive thematic analysis: workforce and operational challenges; AI awareness and readiness; AI as teacher support, not replacement; AI and equity; AI and learning quality; and responsible AI adoption. Participants considered how AI could support planning, documentation, translation, administration, and personalised learning, freeing up time for meaningful teacher–child interaction. They stressed, however, that AI cannot address structural workforce shortages and cannot take the place of teachers’ relational, professional, and safeguarding roles. The study’s contribution lies in bringing together workforce, equity, learn-ing quality, and responsible AI adoption within a single ECE-focused empirical framework, and in highlighting the necessity of human-centred implementation. Longitudinal and mixed-methods studies in various settings are needed to inves-tigate the impact of AI on teacher workload, child outcomes, equity, and policy implementation.

item.title: Teachers’ experiences with generative AI for lesson planning: A qualitative study in Sindh, Pakistan
item.description:
Perspectives in Social Sciences
This Qualitative descriptive study explored how 15 in service Junior Elementary School teachers (JESTs) at Government Higher Secondary School Dad Laghari, Sindh, Pakistan, described their familiarity and use of artificial intelligence (GenAI) for lesson planning, perceived benefits and challenges, and professional learning and support needs. Participants provided written English responses to five open ended questions and profile information. Responses were analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis and participant characteristics were summarized descriptively. From the study five themes were identified like Familiarity with GenAI and reported planning uses; perceived efficiency and expanded planning options; verification of generated materials for accuracy and classroom fit; integration of AI fluency with subject and pedagogical knowledge ; and collegial and institutional support. Teachers reported using GenAI to draft lesson notes, questions, activities, examples, and explanations. Thirteen reported frequent use, while two reported occasional use. Participants showed concerns about accuracy, curriculum and learner suitability, privacy and internet access and identified need for practical training, peer exchange, digital resources and school guidance. The findings highlights self reported perspective from one school; lesson plan, classroom practice and student outcomes were not assessed.

item.title: Overview of the Current State and Prospects of Artificial Intelligence
item.description:
Journal of Research in Engineering and Computer Sciences
Between 2023 and 2026, artificial intelligence (AI) reached a decisive stage of development. From language models capable of logical reasoning to autonomous agents able to carry out complex tasks, AI is redefining the boundaries of productivity, creativity, and employment. This review provides a broad overview of AI in 2026, covering its core technologies, major market participants, practical impacts, and ethical challenges, while examining the current state of the field and its likely future direction.

item.title: La “creatività” dell’IA e le sue proprietà: definizioni e criticità nell’era dei LLM
item.description:
AI-Linguistica Linguistic Studies on AI-Generated Texts and Discourses
Il concetto di “creatività”, virtù spesso attribuita all’intelletto o alla fantasia dell’essere umano, è di recente divenuto oggetto di trattazione all’interno di testi scientifici sull’IA. Per tale motivo, diversi ambiti di ricerca si preoccupano di definire una nuova ontologia della creatività che prenda in considerazione la continua evoluzione di sistemi artificiali come i LLM. In linea con tali sviluppi, la presente ricerca propone una definizione critica della creatività nell’ambito dell’IA, basata sui cinque elementi fondamentali della creatività: agente (actor), processo (process), prodotto (outcome), dominio (domain) e spazio (space). Una successiva analisi quantitativo-qualitativa basata su corpus riflette poi sugli usi linguistici dell’aggettivo creative in testi di computer science ad alto rigore scientifico e sulla sua co-occorrenza in relazione a termini riguardanti i cinque elementi fondamentali, classificati secondo la ricerca di Wingström et al. (2022).

item.title: AI-DRIVEN, EVIDENCE-BASED GENERATIVE DESIGN: A TEACHING FRAMEWORK FOR LANDSCAPE ARCHITECTONICS INTEGRATING RESEARCH FINDINGS, DESIGN PRECEDENTS, AND INTELLIGENT RECOGNITION AND JUDGMENT
item.description:
World Journal of Educational Studies
Artificial intelligence (AI) has entered design courses, but its use often stops at tool operation. Taking Landscape Architectonics, an undergraduate course in landscape architecture programs, as the vehicle, this paper builds a teaching framework for generative design that integrates four elements: research findings, design precedents, AI-based recognition and judgment, and AI generation. The core claim is simple. Teaching students to “use AI” means teaching them to run an evidence-constrained generative design chain. “AI-driven” therefore carries two meanings: at the tool level, AI executes generation; at the teaching level, evidence steers generation, and the work of teaching lies in leading students from the former toward the latter. Among the four elements, research findings and design precedents are static knowledge that travels across sites. Research findings supply criteria for what counts as good. Design precedents supply examples of what to do, distilled from 13 street design guidelines into 114 retrievable situation packages. AI-based recognition and AI generation produce dynamic outputs anchored to a specific site. Students mobilize these elements through three stages—reading the site, grounding the context, and giving form—and a chain of evidence disciplines each stage. The framework follows three design principles: complementary elements, partial embedding, and explicit judgment. Three classroom examples show how the framework operates. This paper focuses on framework construction and does not report learning-outcome data.

item.title: Automated Language Sample Analysis for Argentine Spanish-Speaking Children: Evaluating ASR and NLP Pipelines Against Expert Transcriptions
item.description:
[预印本] Figshare
AbstractPurpose: Narrative production tasks offer a rich context for assessing children's oral language development, but manual language sample analysis remains time-intensive. This study evaluates the accuracy of automated speech recognition (ASR) and natural language processing (NLP) pipelines for recovering 16 linguistic metrics from narrative productions of Argentine Spanish-speaking children.Method: The corpus comprised 54 recordings from 16 children aged 4–8 years. Following manual audio preprocessing, measures were computed from manual or Whisper Turbo transcripts using automated word-class annotation. For utterance-level measures, local and cloud-based large language models (LLMs) segmented communication units (C-units), with punctuation-based segmentation serving as a baseline. Performance was assessed using Pearson correlations and median absolute relative errors.Results: Despite a mean ASR word error rate of 29.3%, broad lexical and content-word measures showed strong correlations with expert values (r = .988–.999) and median errors of 1.1%–8.0% on ASR transcripts of child narratives. Some grammatical-category diversity measures showed larger relative errors. Cloud-based LLM segmentation of ASR transcripts reduced median errors for C-unit counts and longest-utterance measures compared with punctuation-based segmentation. Mean length of utterance in words showed inconsistent and less reliable performance, including weak correlations on ASR transcripts.Conclusions: Selected linguistic metrics can be recovered from children's Argentine Spanish spontaneous narratives despite transcription errors. LLM-based C-unit segmentation is a promising approach for languages and populations underrepresented in ASR training data, but it is still metric-dependent. Practical recommendations for low-cost implementation in educational and clinical settings are discussed.

item.title: Exploratory data analysis and machine learning-based assessment of social media addiction and its impact on academic performance and mental health among students
item.description:
[预印本] Figshare
This study investigates social media addiction among students. It includes definitions, ways to measure it, how common it is, and its effects on mental health and academic performance. A focused review of literature from 2018 to 2025 gathers systematic reviews, meta-analyses, psychometric studies, and research that connects problematic social media use to issues like mental health problems, sleep disruptions, and academic results. The article also provides a method for analyzing student-level social media addiction data. It discusses common findings in datasets and offers recommendations for educators and policymakers based on evidence. Using data from 705 participants across 110 countries, this study combines a thorough literature review, dataset-driven exploratory data analysis (EDA), and correlational modeling. The results show strong connections between social media addiction, academic success, sleep, and mental health. The EDA reveals gender differences in usage, regional differences in platform preferences, and clear links between addiction and poorer sleep quality and mental health. These findings align with global research and suggest the potential value of targeted digital well-being interventions among students.

item.title: Transformative learning in farmer research networks: insights from Eastern and Southern Africa
item.description:
[预印本] Figshare
Farmer research networks are collaborative platforms where farmers, researchers, extension workers, and NGOs co-create knowledge, experiment with innovations, and tackle local challenges through joint learning and action. Although interest in these networks is growing, there remains a limited understanding of how learning occurs within them. This study draws on qualitative data from nine networks active between 2015 and 2024 in Kenya, Malawi and Uganda. It reveals that these networks foster individual and collective transformation. The process is dynamic, multi-dimensional, technical, relational, and emotional, shaped by diverse knowledge systems and social interactions. Emotional engagement , enhanced motivation, deepened reflection, and prompted identity shifts. Networks function not only as sites of knowledge co-creation and learning but also as cultural and emotional spaces where agricultural visions and identities are negotiated and reshaped. Farmers assumed roles as researchers and educators, adapting agroecological innovations and experimenting with solutions to ecological and livelihood challenges. The key enabling factors were trust among members, inclusive facilitation, institutional memory, and strong local leadership. Progress was constrained by entrenched gender norms, hierarchical extension practices, and rigid social structures. Sustaining transformative learning calls for continued investment in facilitation capacity, inclusive leadership and institutional structures that embed networks within broader innovation systems.

item.title: Constraining the Commit Boundary: A DIO/ODI-Informed Authorization Guardrail for Agentic Entity Resolution
item.description:
[预印本] Figshare
This paper proposes a Digital Identity Optimization (DIO) and Ontology of Digital Identity (ODI)-informed authorization guardrail for persistent identity-changing mutations in Agentic Entity Resolution (ER).Agentic ER systems iteratively plan actions, retrieve evidence, update hypotheses, and propose graph mutations. An erroneous identity hypothesis may therefore condition subsequent evidence acquisition and produce observations that appear to confirm the original error. The paper does not claim to eliminate this feedback mechanism. Instead, it distinguishes evidence available to an agent for reasoning from evidence eligible to authorize a persistent change to an entity’s identity.The proposed architecture connects selected DIO/ODI reconstruction-failure distinctions—referential, semantic, temporal, and contextual—to domain-configured identity-preserving constraints. A diagnostic-to-constraint mapping specifies which identity or continuity propositions a mutation must establish, which relations are insufficient to establish them, and when temporal applicability, contextual requirements, or unresolved conflicts call for deferral.An abstract two-phase Minimum Viable Digital Identity Optimization (MVDIO) Supervisor Layer separates evidence admission, claim-specific promotion, and protected graph commitment. Admission as UNVERIFIED permits exploratory reasoning but does not confer authorization eligibility. Evidence becomes eligible only for the proposition, evidentiary role, and applicability established under the declared policy. A persistent mutation may be committed only when the candidate graph satisfies the applicable constraints, each required proposition has appropriate claim-specific support, no unresolved material conflict blocks authorization, the operation remains within its authorized scope, and the relevant state and policy versions remain valid at commit time.The paper develops this contract through a lifecycle-to-boundary analysis, a stylized model of apparent verification, an authorization invariant with explicit assumptions, abstract interface algorithms, and hypothetical corporate entity-resolution cases. A prospective evaluation protocol distinguishes the proposed DIO/ODI-informed mapping from conventional identifier rules, conservative abstention, and a generic authorization boundary configured from the same domain facts.The contribution is an explicit specification of commit-boundary obligations, not a new matching algorithm, a stand-alone theorem of semantic correctness, or an implemented and empirically validated system. Its property remains conditional on domain-policy adequacy, claim-specific evidence promotion, recorded-provenance integrity, and enforcement of the protected boundary. The incremental value of the DIO/ODI diagnostic organization remains an open empirical question. Broader dependency-aware control of hypothesis-conditioned evidence acquisition and feedback is identified as a separate research direction. Canonical archival version: The canonical archival version of this preprint is deposited in Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23580733. AI disclosure: This paper was developed through a human-led, model-assisted process of conceptual exploration, source-oriented research, architectural formulation, drafting, formalization, and adversarial review. GPT-based systems, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity, Qwen, and Kimi contributed in different roles during development. Model outputs were treated as fallible proposals and critiques, not as independent peer review or evidence of system performance. The author selected, rejected, and revised suggestions and retains responsibility for the framing, design decisions, interpretations, claims, references, and final text. A detailed methodological disclosure is included in the manuscript.

item.title: Pemanfaatan Artificial Intelligence untuk Penguatan Branding Digital UMKM dalam Meningkatkan Daya Saing Produk Lokal
item.description:
Journal of Community Service and Society Empowerment
Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) are the main pillars of the Indonesian economy, but most micro-scale business actors face limited resources in managing their businesses. The main problem faced by the service partners, namely Sahabat Genggam Teman Indonesia (GTI), which facilitates MSME administrators in Bekasi City, is low literacy. Branding is digital, with less-than-optimal brand identity elements, minimal use of Artificial Intelligence (AI), and limited resources to obtain professional assistance. This Community Service (PKM) activity aims to improve partners' literacy and skills in using AI technology, particularly ChatGPT as an AI branding assistant, to independently design brand names, slogans, brand positioning, product descriptions, and social media copy. The activity will be carried out independently in a hybrid format at the Grand Metropolitan Bekasi Ballroom and via Zoom Meeting on October 13, 2026. The implementation method includes surveys and problem identification, material/module preparation, educational training with lectures and interactive discussions, and evaluation. The outcome of this activity is increased knowledge and skills among partners, in this case MSMEs, enabling them to operate and use ChatGPT as an AI branding assistant to design brand names, slogans, brand positioning, product descriptions, and copywriting independently for social media. This activity helps MSMEs streamline their operations and product marketing.

item.title: On Multilingual Text Summarization: A Review of Model Architectures, Techniques, and Research Gaps
item.description:
International Journal of Data Informatics and Intelligent Computing
The rapid expansion of multilingual digital content has intensified demand for automated text summarization systems that can operate across diverse languages. Yet the architectural and methodological foundations of this domain remain dispersed across individual studies. This paper presents a systematic literature review of multilingual text summarization research in Natural Language Processing, with particular attention to model architectures, multilingual enabling techniques, and existing research gaps. Following a PRISMA-guided review protocol, 47 studies published between 2017 and 2026 were identified, screened, and synthesized from major scholarly databases using predefined eligibility and quality assessment criteria. The analysis shows that the literature is dominated by four dominant architectural paradigms: multilingual sequence-to-sequence models, large language models, adapter-based models, and hybrid architectures, with a recent shift toward large language model-based approaches. Across these studies, multilingual capability is primarily achieved through pre-training and transfer learning, with support from parameter-efficient adaptation and data augmentation. The review further identified four persistent limitation categories: low-resource language underrepresentation; dataset and benchmark constraints; evaluation limitations dominated by ROUGE overreliance; and generalization and scalability challenges, manifested as the curse of multilinguality. These findings indicate that current progress in the field is largely driven by scaling existing models rather than resolving structural multilingual limitations, particularly those related to data availability and model architecture. This paper provides a consolidated view of architectural and methodological trends and offers a structured, informed basis for future research on equitable multilingual summarization, particularly for low-resource languages.

item.title: EXPERIENTIAL AND EMBODIED LEARNING IN SPECIAL EDUCATION UNDER NEP 2020: CONFERENCE PROCEEDINGS
item.description:
mLAC Journal for Arts Commerce and Sciences (m-JACS)
These proceedings bring together 51 conference abstracts presented in connection with the Two-Day Symposium on “Experiential and Embodied Learning in Special Education under NEP 2020: Conference Proceedings,” scheduled for 22–23 October 2026 at the Regional Institute of Education (NCERT), Mysuru. The collection explores inclusive education and experiential learning through themes including theatre and art-based pedagogy, yogic and embodied learning, inclusive science and mathematics education, teacher education, multilingual learning, digital technologies, artificial intelligence, accessibility, and learner well-being. In the context of the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020, the proceedings provide a forum for academic exchange on approaches intended to make teaching and learning more participatory, accessible, and responsive to diverse learners, including learners with disabilities. The contributions reflect a range of topics and proposed approaches; the present abstract summarises the scope of the collection and does not claim that the proceedings establish a single set of empirical findings.

item.title: Problem analysis of curriculum development for application-oriented undergraduate art and design programs in Chinese-foreign cooperative education: a case study
item.description:
Forum for education studies.
Based on the OBE (Outcome-Based Education) philosophy, this study examines the construction of curriculum systems for application-oriented undergraduate art and design programs in Chinese-foreign cooperative education, taking the Modern International Art & Design Academy of Chongqing Technology and Business University as a case study. The research identifies four core challenges in practice at present: a gap between application-oriented talent cultivation goals and OBE principles; an incomplete curriculum system that integrates local needs with an international perspective; a dual-standard issue in assessment and evaluation systems oriented toward students’ long-term career development; and the absence of an effective collaborative mechanism between Chinese and foreign faculty despite their physical co-presence. These problems essentially reflect the structural tension between internationalization and localization. The study proposes that the solution lies in constructing a new educational logic of integrated co-creation, applying an outcome-oriented approach throughout the entire process of goal setting, curriculum reconstruction, evaluation reform, and faculty development. This approach would promote the organic integration of international design education resources with local industry-education collaboration, and establish a career competency tracking and support system that runs through the entire cultivation process. This study also provides a problem definition and analytical framework for similar institutions seeking to advance high-quality development in Chinese-foreign cooperative education.

item.title: Teachers’ Moral Resilience in the Digital Era: Internalizing Professional Codes and Islamic Moral Values
item.description:
Journal of Multidisciplinary Science MIKAILALSYS
Digital education presents ethical challenges requiring teachers to exercise moral judgment, maintain integrity, and demonstrate professional accountability. Discussions of professional codes often emphasize regulation, giving insufficient attention to their internalization as foundations for moral resilience and professional identity. This study examines how professional codes, moral principles, Islamic ethical values, and personal values can be conceptually integrated to strengthen teachers’ ethical responsibilities in the digital era. A qualitative literature review synthesized academic books, scholarly articles, and relevant educational policy documents through descriptive analysis, thematic classification, and conceptual interpretation. The synthesis distinguishes four interconnected dimensions: ethics grounds rational moral judgment; morality articulates socially recognized standards of conduct; akhlak emphasizes spiritual integrity and exemplary behavior; and internalized values support consistency in professional decisions. Their integration provides a conceptual account of moral resilience that connects professional obligations with ethical reasoning and personal commitment. Digital privacy, artificial intelligence, institutional pressures, and the commercialization of education emerge as important contexts for applying this perspective. The study contributes an integrative understanding of professional codes as resources for moral responsibility, ethical reasoning, and professional identity formation. It recommends incorporating reflective ethical case studies, professional mentoring, and ethical training responsive to educational contexts into teacher preparation and continuing professional development.

item.title: BLOCKCHAIN-DRIVEN VERIFICATION OF AI-GENERATED DIGITAL CONTENT
item.description:
International Journal of Progressive Research in Engineering Management and Science
The rapid growth of generative artificial intelligence has altered how digital content is created.Images, videos, audio, documents, and text can now be produced or modified with relatively minimal technical knowledge.These advances benefit areas such as education, communication, entertainment, business, and research, but they also introduce a practical issue: it is increasingly difficult to determine where a digital file originated and whether it was modified later.Existing ai detectors are able to identify some synthetic or manipulated content; however, their ability to do so may vary depending on the emergence of new generation models or when a file undergoes size alteration, compression, editing, or sharing across different platforms.This paper introduces a blockchain-driven framework that enables verification of the provenance and integrity of ai-generated digital content.The proposed framework integrates several key components including ai-based content analysis, cryptographic hashing, perceptual fingerprinting, digital signatures, decentralized identity, smart contracts, and blockchain-based provenance records.Instead of storing entire media files onto the blockchain, the system stores compact verification metadata on-chain and stores the actual content in an appropriate off-chain storage.When verifying a submitted file, the file is hashed and compared to the registered record.In addition, ai analysis is utilized as an additional form of evidence regarding potential synthetic generation or manipulation.This paper describes the architecture, verification process, security considerations, advantages, limitations, possible methods of evaluation, and future directions for the proposed framework.

item.title: ChatGPT-assisted mathematics learning in the era of generative AI: A bibliometric analysis of research trends, collaboration networks, and emerging pedagogical themes
item.description:
International Journal of Mathematics and Mathematics Education
Purpose – This study aims to map the development of research on ChatGPT-assisted mathematics learning during the 2023–2025 period. Methodology – This study uses bibliometric analysis to examine the intellectual, social, and conceptual structures of research on ChatGPT-assisted mathematics learning. Data were obtained from the Scopus database and analyzed using Bibliometrix Biblioshiny. Document selection followed the PRISMA 2020 reporting guidelines as a checklist for the identification, screening, eligibility, and inclusion stages. Of the 1,227 documents identified, 143 met the inclusion criteria and were analyzed further. Findings – The number of publications increased from 12 in 2023 to 36 in 2024 and 95 in 2025, indicating an annual growth rate of 181.37% and an average of 18.63 citations per document. International co-authorship accounted for only 16.78% of these documents, indicating limited cross-national collaboration. ChatGPT, mathematics education, and artificial intelligence were the most dominant keywords, while geometry, prospective mathematics teachers, and personalized learning were relatively underrepresented. Novelty – Unlike previous studies that generally treat ChatGPT as part of generative artificial intelligence, this research analytically positions ChatGPT-assisted mathematics learning as a separate bibliometric unit and proposes AI-mediated mathematics learning as a conceptual proposition that emphasizes critical validation of AI-generated results. Significance – These findings provide an evidence-based research agenda to strengthen international collaboration and develop mathematics instruction that emphasizes reasoning, justification, and critical evaluation of AI-generated solutions, while identifying priorities for future empirical research.

Nordic Machine Intelligence
NORA - The Norwegian Artificial Intelligence Research Consortium - works to strengthen Norwegian research, education and innovation within the fields of AI, machine learning and robotics. NORA is a collaboration between 9 universities, 4 university colleges and 4 research institutes. The current article provides a summary of NORA’s annual conference 2026.

item.title: BEYOND TECHNOSTRESS AI Fatigue as a Cumulative Adaptation Burden in Education and Work
item.description:
Emirati Journal of Applied Psychology
Artificial intelligence has become a persistent layer of work and learning rather than an occasional tool. Users must repeatedly decide when to delegate, how to prompt, whether to trust, how to verify, and how responsibility should be distributed. This integrative review defines AI fatigue as a cumulative reduction in the cognitive, affective, or motivational capacity for adaptive AI engagement when interaction, evaluation, correction, learning, and role-adjustment demands accumulate faster than recovery and support. The review connects technostress, automation vigilance, cognitive load and offloading, trust calibration, digital fatigue, and the Job Demands–Resources perspective. It introduces an Exposure–Adaptation–Depletion–Response framework, a five-domain taxonomy, and an AI Fatigue Load model that separates use volume from uncertainty, task stakes, correction burden, interruption, role disruption, and imposed adoption velocity. The analysis is updated to incorporate a 2026 validated 15-item AI Fatigue Scale; the proposed load model complements that psychophysiological outcome measure by specifying socio-technical antecedents and exposure conditions. Educational and organizational applications show why AI may simultaneously improve output and worsen human sustainability. The article identifies recurring inferential errors, presents a measurement and longitudinal research agenda, and proposes an intervention hierarchy spanning interface design, workflow, curriculum, organizational policy, and governance. AI fatigue is positioned neither as generic screen tiredness nor as a synonym for burnout, but as an adaptation problem located in the coupled human–AI–institution system.

item.title: Student Perceptions of Artificial Intelligence and Metaverse-Enabled Remote Learning in New Zealand Tertiary Education
item.description:
International Journal of Higher Education
The increasing development of emerging digital technologies is creating new possibilities for remote tertiary education. Artificial Intelligence and Metaverse technologies offer potential for personalised learning, intelligent support, immersive interaction, and collaboration; however, their educational value depends partly on how students perceive their usefulness, accessibility, supporting conditions, and motivational potential. This study examined New Zealand tertiary students’ perceptions of prospective Artificial Intelligence- and Metaverse-enabled remote learning environments and investigated whether selected technology-acceptance and motivational factors were associated with perceived learning engagement. A mono-method quantitative, cross-sectional survey design was adopted. Data were collected through an online questionnaire comprising 20 Likert-scale items representing six constructs: performance expectancy, facilitating conditions, motivation, perceived ease of use, perceived usefulness, and perceived learning engagement. A total of 356 responses were retained for analysis. Descriptive statistics, reliability analysis, Pearson correlation, exploratory chi-square analysis, and multiple linear regression were conducted. The regression model was statistically significant and explained 33.8% of the variance in perceived learning engagement (R² = .338; adjusted R² = .329; F = 35.773, p < .001). Perceived usefulness (β = .279, p < .001), motivation (β = .218, p < .001), and facilitating conditions (β = .179, p < .001) were statistically significant predictors of perceived learning engagement. Performance expectancy (β = .065, p = .223) and perceived ease of use (β = .089, p = .058) were not statistically significant predictors. An exploratory chi-square analysis also identified a statistically significant association between age and perceptions of virtual teamwork (p = .001). The findings provide preliminary evidence that perceived usefulness, motivation, and facilitating conditions are important considerations in understanding student engagement with prospective advanced remote learning environments. Given the cross-sectional design and purposive non-probability sampling, the findings indicate statistical associations rather than causal effects and should be interpreted within the study sample.

item.title: ЛАКУНАРНОСТЬ В ХУДОЖЕСТВЕННОМ ТЕКСТЕ: ЭКСПЛИЦИТНЫЕ И ИМПЛИЦИТНЫЕ АСПЕКТЫ
item.description:
Вестник Адыгейского государственного университета серия «Филология и искусствоведение»
В статье рассматривается феномен лакунарности как фундаментального принципа организации художественного текста, обеспечивающего его смысловую глубину и эстетическую ценность. Анализируются два взаимосвязанных аспекта лакунарности: эксплицитный, связанный со структурными пропусками в повествовании (композиционные разрывы, диалогические паузы, темпоральные скачки, синтаксические эллипсисы), и имплицитный, отвечающий за генерацию скрытых смыслов (психологический, идейно-философский и культурно-аксиологический подтекст). На материале романа У. Теккерея «Ярмарка тщеславия» демонстрируется, что взаимодействие выраженного и невыраженного активизирует читательское восприятие, превращая чтение в процесс сотворчества. Доказывается, что лакунарность является не случайным элементом, а строго организованной системой, повышающей интерпретационный потенциал текста и обеспечивающей его многозначность. The article examines the phenomenon of lacunarity as a fundamental principle of the organization of a literary text, ensuring its semantic depth and aesthetic value. Two interrelated aspects of lacunarity are analyzed: the explicit one, associated with structural gaps in the narrative (compositional breaks, dialogical pauses, temporal jumps, syntactic ellipses), and the implicit one, responsible for generating hidden meanings (psychological, ideological, philosophical, and cultural-axiological overtones). Based on the novel by U. Thackeray «Vanity Fair» it demonstrates that the interaction of the expressed and the unexpressed activates the reader's perception, turning reading into a process of co-creation. It is proved that lacunarity is not an accidental element, but a strictly organized system that increases the interpretative potential of the text and ensures its ambiguity.
